analysis.title: SetNotu: Antrenman Formu ve İlerleme Günlüğü
analysis.summary: Krato, form ipuçları ve egzersiz kütüphanesiyle ayda 362,95 dolar ciro bildiriyor; bu kâr veya Türkiye talebi kanıtı değil. Hipotez, set sonrası kısa form notları ve basit ilerleme çizelgesi sunan mobil bir günlük.

analysis.problem: Antrenman yapanlar ağırlığı kaydeder ancak hareket formunu, tekrar kalitesini ve gelişimi birlikte takip etmekte zorlanır. Hedef, antrenman sonrası 20 saniyelik notlarla bu boşluğu doldurmaktır.
analysis.turkishAngle: Türk kullanıcı arayüzü, metrik ağırlık birimi ve sade antrenman terimleri kullanılacak. Türkiye talebi bilinmediğinden hipotez yalnızca yerel kullanıcı görüşmeleriyle test edilecek.
features: Antrenman sonrası 20 saniyelik form notu ve tekrar kalitesi seçimi.
Egzersize göre set, ağırlık ve gelişim çizelgesi.
Hareket adı, kısa form ipucu ve sık hata kütüphanesi.
firstCustomers: İstanbul, Ankara ve İzmir'deki 3 bağımsız salonun Instagram hesaplarına doğrudan ulaşarak 10 antrenman yapan kişiden görüşme ve ön sipariş iste.
Antrenman içerikleri paylaşan Türkçe Instagram hesaplarına, takipçilerine yönelik 10 kişilik kısa test grubu öner.
Üniversite spor kulüplerinin WhatsApp topluluklarında 48 saatlik prototip görüşmesi duyur.
validation: İlk 24 saatte 10 hedef kullanıcı bul; en az 5'i form takibini öncelikli sorun olarak doğrulasın.
İkinci 24 saatte 5 kullanıcı prototipi tamamlasın; en az 3'ü 7 günlük kullanıma başlasın.
En az 5 ön sipariş veya depozito alınamazsa teklifi durdur.
Ortalama kayıt süresi 45 saniyenin üzerindeyse akışı sadeleştir veya durdur.
analysis.stopCondition: 48 saatte en az 10 hedef kullanıcıyla görüş. 5 kişi ön sipariş veya depozito vermezse, 3 kullanıcı 7 günlük günlük kullanımı tamamlamazsa veya ortalama kayıt süresi 45 saniyeyi aşarsa dur.
unknowns: Türkiye'de kullanıcı talebi, ödeme isteği ve uygun fiyat bilinmiyor.
Egzersiz ve form içeriklerinin doğruluğu ile güncellenmesi için uzman desteği gerekiyor olabilir.
Mobil mağaza onayı, müşteri edinme maliyeti ve kullanıcı edinim kanalları bilinmiyor.
Kişisel sağlık verisi işlenecekse açık rıza ve veri güvenliği gereksinimleri belirlenmeli.
Rakip yokluğu doğrulanmadı; Krato ve benzeri uygulamalar karşılaştırılmalı.

builder.basis: Dayanak: Krato'nun açıklanan mobil form kütüphanesi, egzersiz takibi ve ciro beyanı; ölçek: tek geliştirici, küçük bir mobil MVP ve ilk 10 kullanıcı. Belirsizlikler: fiyat, Türkiye talebi, içerik doğruluğu, mağaza süreci, müşteri edinme ve rakipler bilinmiyor.

cards.title: Show HN: Foremerge – Catch Intent Conflicts Between Parallel Coding Agents

signals.title: Show HN: Foremerge – Catch Intent Conflicts Between Parallel Coding Agents
signals.description:
At, GPTree, we run several coding agents across our team on one repo using parallel worktrees. Apart from wasted time reviewing and fixing conflicts at PR time, the failures that hurt the most are when multiple plans or tickets cause architecture changes that cannot both be true. Ex. one agent replaces a class while another one is in the process of extending it. Git only notices if the resulting patches happen to touch the same lines and the review only catches it if they are familiar with both tickets.

Foremerge is a local "git like" coordination layer that sits above git (ie. does not interact with or change the way git and worktrees function), Before editing each agent publishes an intent and the scopes it will change, with the operation it plans to complete on each one.

    foremerge intent publish --agent "$A" \
        --summary "Replace PaymentService with StripePaymentService" \
        --scope symbol:PaymentService=replace
    foremerge intent publish --agent "$B" \
        --summary "Add PayPal support to PaymentService" \
        --scope symbol:PaymentService=extend
The publish by the 2nd agent returns a HIGH destructive_vs_additive finding before writing any code. Agents keep their own worktrees and the shared state is one SQLite file in gits common direectory. No hooks, no merge drivers, nothing rewrites your history.

It ships as one Rust binary with a CLI and MCP server with 18 tools and `foremerge setup all` wires it into Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. Because the protocol has nothing provider specific, a Claude agent and a Codex agent coordinate through the same store. Before any work is accepted, Foremerge runs a named check that you configured against the exact git state of the change. An agent that says tests pass is recorded but it dosnt satisfy the acceptance gate without running the check itself.

Detection is deterministic, no judge model reading your code. HIGH

cards.title: Show HN: I built a camera that you talk with instead of seeing your own face

signals.title: Show HN: I built a camera that you talk with instead of seeing your own face
signals.description:
I used to hate recording myself, but at the same time I also wanted to post more video i.e. on X.

My usual experience was: Get an idea -> reluctantly hit record -> become self-aware, stumble, do 8 takes -> give up.

So I tried changing the camera instead.

MakiRoll doesn't show you your face while you're recording.

You give it a rough topic and it asks you questions, or lets you ramble.

Those questions adapt to what you've just said via STT and a language model, so recording feels more like having a conversation than performing at a lens.

Once you're done, it looks through the transcript, finds the interesting takes, suggests a structure and makes a captioned cut.

The interesting part for me hasn't really been the editing part, which is nice, but by removing the mirror and replacing it with another participant seems to change how people behave while recording.

One of my early testers described himself as super shy, and now he's making videos and getting more comfortable doing it.

It's built for web + iOS. I'd love some feedback on whether the conversational recording model makes sense to people who normally avoid going on camera (but would like to do that more).

Jev's launch inspired me to work on this project. I had used fine tuned bert models, zero-shot models to achieve jev like functionality in healthcare insurance fraud audits in the last 2-3 years with good results.

Jev's launch showed that there is still market and demand for these type of systems. So I wanted to build a FOSS version which would push the research and tinkering (R&T) in this direction.

Do not use this where decisions can be costly. There's an accuracy/intelligence ceiling with these models no matter what the api seller tells you.

Use this where you can tell the affected party - "oh yeah, sometimes it can mess up" and you both can have a laugh on the expense of machines.

cards.title: Show HN: Accordia – Structured 1-on-1s for engineering managers

signals.title: Show HN: Accordia – Structured 1-on-1s for engineering managers
signals.description:
Hi everyone, I'm a solo developer in Lincolnshire, UK. I've recently built Accordia. It is a 1-on-1 tool for engineering managers. You build a reusable agenda per report, run the meeting against it, and anything that turns into an action gets tracked and pulled into the next session automatically.

I built it because of the 1-on-1s I sat in as a developer, not ones I ran as a manager. The pattern was always the same. The first few were good. Then my manager got busy, the meeting quietly turned into a status update, and something I'd raised in March came back as a surprise in my end of year review. None of them were bad managers but the 1 on 1 was not their priority so it ended up coming from memory and whilst there were good intentions there were issues with the process.

So the thing I'm actually trying to fix isn't manager capability, it's the amount of discipline a good 1-on-1 currently demands. Most of the managers I've spoken to are running theirs out of a Notion doc or a shared spreadsheet. That works fine until it doesn't, and when it stops working nothing tells you until it's too late and you're in a messy situation.

That also means I'm competing with Notion and spreadsheets, not with Lattice or 15Five. There's no performance review cycle, no engagement scoring, no HR dashboard, and direct reports don't need accounts.

A few parts are open with no signup if you want to poke at it before deciding:

The demo - https://www.getaccordia.com/demo,

Agenda generator (no auth, exports to PDF) - https://www.getaccordia.com/1-on-1-agenda-generator,

Question library - https://www.getaccordia.com/1-o

cards.title: Show HN: flyOS – A fruit fly connectome simulated in real time on an iPhone

signals.title: Show HN: flyOS – A fruit fly connectome simulated in real time on an iPhone
signals.description:
Hey HN, I'm Cory. When I saw Google release the fruit fly connectome, I wanted to experiment with it myself and better understand how the fruit fly brain works, so I started hacking on a few different iOS projects.

Originally I was going to create an app that let you experience BEING a fruit fly with VR, but then I realized that a fruit fly's main sense is its smell, and an iPhone can't smell. So I ended up building an app based on all of the senses an iPhone has that we could wire to a fruit fly. I came up with flyOS: basically the camera is its eyes, the CPU is its brain, etc. The neuron simulator is written from scratch in Swift and runs in real time on the phone's CPU, with no server involved.

Yes, this is partly a joke. But it's also a serious app that lets you view the neurons of a simulated fly in real time, which I think is pretty cool. I wrote a white paper and put it online to share the process of building this, and why I ultimately only ended up using 4,895 neurons out of the total 166,000 in the release.

Would love your feedback and thoughts as to how I could make the fly even more realistic and alive.

nanosamur.ai is a speech-to-tech platform that supports different models for realtime, semi-realtime, and batch transcription and provides a unified stack for robust speech processing, agentic workflows, and webhooks.

You can run it locally on your computer via electron app + docker compose, but you can take the same stack and run it in cloud/k8s and/or on prem as it is built with scale in mind (it also has an observability stack built in). So in that sense it is more like Ollama + Ollama Cloud :)

Currently it supports whisper, qwen asr, nemotron asr and parakeet tdt and I am adding other models. I am also adding Kserve+Triton integration for the batch transcriptions so as the MLOps can be abstracted away.

Last couple of years I have been consulting for some organizations that work with sensitive data and have to keep them in air gapped environments and based on those experiences I built and open-sourced nanosamur.ai

The easiest place to start is the main repo: https://github.com/nanosamurai/nanosamurai

It is a docker compose starter setup, there are couple of services it uses, all are linked in the documentation; I used python for the voice ai services (see the xamurai monorepo) and java / clojure / clojurescript for the UI/BFF and some other services (yes, it is pg's fault i love lisps).

Appreciate any feedback! Esp. from people working with speech infrastructure, self hosted AI etc. Also it currently sits at 6 stars, so feel free to star the repos if you like them :)

signals.title: Show HN: Sommelier, an Excel Addin for your agent
signals.description:
Sommelier (there is a nice wordplay on Excel and pairing) is an Excel Addin + relay server that lets your agent work hand in hand with you while you're working on an Excel spreadsheet. It's heavily inspired by the excellent marimo pair.

It's useful when you either don't want to use Microsoft Copilot, want to use a local model + harness for security reason, or want to use an agent that already has access to personal data.

I've tested it with some harnesses (pi, opencode, codex) but I guess that it should work on many others.

Not having a Microsoft developer account, I've yet to publish it to the marketplace, but it's sideloadable.

While the first prototype was written by me, I've only kept the core and let an LLM rewrite the code.

signals.description:

I'm a big fan of cognitive games like Human Benchmark and brain games in general.

I'm also a big fan of Trackmania's leaderboard system, where you can compete globally or by continent, country, region, etc.

So I thought, why not combine the two?

I ended up building Human Rank, a collection of 10 games with global and regional leaderboards.

I'd love to get some feedback and also compete with you guys if you want :)

I'm thinking of creating a discord as well if there are people linking the same things (don't know if it's a good idea tho)

Max.
